items.stem: The fully loaded cost of an employee is best described as:

options.text: Gross salary plus all employer on-costs such as employer taxes, pension and benefits
options.rationale: Correct: fully loaded cost adds employer-borne costs to gross pay.
Net pay understates the cost to the employer.
Deductions withheld are not the total cost.

items.explanation: Correct: fully loaded cost adds employer-borne costs to gross pay.
items.provenance: original Mastemy item drafted by an AI agent; no external question source

items.stem: Which TWO controls best reduce payroll fraud risk? (Select TWO.)

options.text: Independent review and approval of all new starters and pay changes
options.rationale: Correct: approval of master-data changes blocks ghost employees and unauthorised raises.

options.text: Segregating payroll preparation from bank payment authorisation
options.rationale: Correct: segregation stops one person creating and paying a fictitious employee.

options.text: Letting the payroll clerk also open and close bank accounts
options.rationale: This concentrates incompatible duties and raises fraud risk.
Reconciliation is a key detective control.

items.explanation: Correct: approval of master-data changes blocks ghost employees and unauthorised raises.

items.stem: Statutory payroll deductions withheld from employees represent, before remittance:

options.text: A liability the employer owes to the relevant authority
options.rationale: Correct: withheld amounts are held in trust and owed onward, a liability.
Withholdings are not the employer's income.
They are the employee's money withheld, not an employer expense.

options.text: An asset the employer may keep
options.rationale: The employer must remit them; they are not retained.

items.explanation: Correct: withheld amounts are held in trust and owed onward, a liability.
